para.text: The purpose of this chapter is to enact regulations that protect and promote the public health and safety of individuals at public spas and pools in the State. Public pools include limited public-use pools, recreational pools, and semipublic pools. Public spas include semipublic spas.

This chapter establishes minimum criteria for the operation and maintenance of all public pools and spas, and construction and design standards for public pools and spas built and in operation before December 31, 2023.
In this chapter:
Absent a definition in §B of this regulation, all of the terms in the International Swimming Pool and Spa Code (ISPSC) apply; and
The following terms have the meanings indicated.
Terms Defined.
Alteration.
“Alteration” means to:
Change or modify an equipment room, a bathhouse, a component, or the configuration of a pool or spa;
Move a component from one location or position to another; or
Install a new component.
“Alteration” does not include a repair or replacement.
“Approved” means found by the Secretary to be in satisfactory compliance with applicable statutes and regulations promulgated or enforced by the Secretary.
“Barrier” means an uninterrupted obstacle intended to prevent direct access from one point to another surrounding and securing a pool or spa.
“Cfm” means cubic feet per minute.
“Component” means:
A piece of pool or spa equipment;
A deck;
A barrier;
One or more skimmers;
One or more filters, including piping and valves;
A ventilation system;
Lighting provided for water, deck, and walkways; or
Pipe material for pool or spa water.
Critical Violation.

“Critical violation” means a violation that results from a product, practice, circumstance, or event that creates a situation that requires immediate correction or cessation of operation to prevent injury, illness, or death based on the number of potential injuries and the nature, severity, and duration of the anticipated injury or illness.
“Critical violation” includes the violations enumerated in Regulation .24A of this chapter.
“Full compliance inspection” means an inspection that verifies compliance with this chapter.
“Hand feeding” means adding chemicals to a pool or spa by any means other than an automatic chemical feeder.
“ISPSC” means the International Swimming Pool and Spa Code.
“ISPSC Pool” means a pool that was constructed and approved:
After December 31, 2023; or
Before December 31, 2023, and has undergone a major alteration after December 31, 2023.
“ISPSC Spa” means a spa that was constructed and approved:
After December 31, 2023; or
Before December 31, 2023, and has undergone a major alteration after December 31, 2023.
“Legacy pool” means a pool that:
Was constructed and approved before December 31, 2023; and
Has not undergone any major alterations after December 31, 2023.
“Legacy spa” means a spa that:
Was constructed and approved before December 31, 2023; and
Has not undergone any major alterations after December 31, 2023.
“Lifeguard” means an individual who is 15 years old or older and who has a valid lifeguard certificate from:
The American Red Cross;
The Boy Scouts of America, not including a lifeguard merit badge;
The YMCA;
Ellis and Associates' National Pool and Waterpark Lifeguard Training; or
An organization with a lifesaving training program equivalent to that of the American Red Cross.
Limited Public-Use Pool.
“Limited public-use pool” means a private pool which is made available for use by:
Children in family day care under the care of a family day care provider at a family day care home as defined in COMAR 13A.15.01.02; or
An organized group, agency, or other person for swimming lessons or water safety training.
“Limited public-use pool” does not include a pool that is emptied of water, disinfected, and refilled with water between each use.
“Major alteration” has the same meaning as “substantial and material structural change” stated in COMAR 09.12.56.04
Major Violation.
“Major violation” means a violation that if not corrected within 24 hours could lead to injury, illness, or death.
“Major violation” includes the violations enumerated in Regulation .24B of this chapter.
“Make-up water” means the potable water used to maintain the water level in a pool or a spa.
“Operator” means a person who supervises, controls, conducts, or manages the operation of a public pool or spa.
Owner.
“Owner” means the owner of a public pool or spa.
“Owner” includes a designee in the form of an operator, builder, management company, or similar entity.
“PHMB” means the disinfectant polyhexamethylene biguanide.

“Pool” means an artificial enclosure of water that is used for the immersion of the human body for recreation, therapy, or exercise, including a structure that is installed in the ground, above ground, outside, or in a building or portable structure.
Private Pool and Private Spa.
“Private pool” and “private spa” mean a pool or spa that is:
Not open to the public;
On a property on which not more than four private residences are located; and
Used exclusively by the residents of the property and nonpaying individuals invited to use the pool or spa by a resident.
“Private pool” and “private spa” include a pool or spa at a private residence used for short-term rentals including weekly, monthly, or seasonal rentals.
Public Pool and Public Spa.
“Public pool” and “public spa” mean a pool or spa that is not a private pool or spa.
“Public pool” includes a:
Limited public-use pool, as defined in §B of this regulation;
Recreational pool as defined in §B of this regulation; and
Semipublic pool, as defined in §B of this regulation.
“Public spa” includes a semipublic spa, as defined in §B of this regulation.
“Recreational pool” means a pool that:
Is not a limited public-use pool, private pool, or semipublic pool, as defined in §B of this regulation;
Is provided as the owner's primary business or the facility's primary purpose, for example, a swim club or similar facility;
Is open for general admission to the public;
Is available to an individual paying a fee for use of the pool;
Is equipped with a sliding board, diving platform, water slide, water flume, or water recreational play equipment that is built into or attached to the pool structure;
Is provided by, or used by a:
Youth camp;
College, university, or school;
Municipality;
Water park, amusement park, or water recreational attraction as defined in §B of this regulation; or
An apartment complex, housing subdivision, or mobile home park with more than ten units, except as provided in §B(28)(a)(v) of this regulation; or
Is used more than 4 times a week for swimming lessons, water safety instruction, or swimming competition;
Meets ISPSC Class A, D, & F;
Meets ISPSC Cass B: except retirement community or marina; or
Meets ISPSC Class C: such as apartment complex, housing subdivision, or mobile home park with more than ten units.
Replacement.

“Replacement” means substituting a component, which has a different make or model but has the same operating characteristics and certifications as the previously approved component, for the previously approved component;
“Replacement” does not include:
Repairs;
Alterations;
Installation of additional equipment; or
Substitutions involving a component which does not meet the requirements of this chapter.
“Secretary” means the Secretary of Health or their designee, including a local health officer.
“Semipublic pool” and “semipublic spa” mean a pool or spa at a facility that:
Has pool use or spa use restricted to an individual:
Staying at the facility, where the facility is a temporary dwelling, including a hotel, motel, campground, bed and breakfast having nine or more guest rooms, or similar temporary dwelling;
Holding membership at the facility, where the facility is an adult health club, retirement community, marina, condominium, or similar facility;
Residing at an apartment complex, housing subdivision, or mobile home park with ten units or less;
Receiving treatment at a physical therapy center pool, or spa, where the pool or spa is used for providing therapy; or
Who is the owner or an owner of the pool or spa; and
Has a pool or spa that is not:
Open for admission to the general public, except as provided in §B(28)(a) of this regulation;
Available to an individual upon the payment of a fee for the use of the pool and spa;
A limited public-use pool, a private pool or a private spa, or a recreational pool, as defined in §B of this regulation;
Equipped with a sliding board, diving platform, water slide, water flume, or water recreational play equipment that is built into or attached to the pool structure; and
At a bed and breakfast that has eight or fewer guest rooms.
Meets ISPSC Class B: retirement community and marina; or
Meets ISPSC Class C: hotels, motels, condominiums, and apartment complex, housing subdivision, or mobile home park with ten units or less.
“Shallow” means, for legacy pools, 5 feet or less in depth.
“Spa” means a pool, hot tub, whirlpool, or ISPSC Class E that is:
Primarily designed for relaxation or therapeutic use and not for swimming;
Not more than 4 feet in depth;
Equipped with built-in seats or benches; and
Usually equipped with hydrotherapy jets, heated or chilled water, an air injection system, or some combination of these features.
“Spray pool” means a shallow pool into which treated water is sprayed but not allowed to accumulate.
“Swimming pool slide” means a device less than 10 feet in height that an individual may use to enter a pool by sliding down an inclined plane.
“Swim spa” means a spa designed to create a current of water against which an individual may swim for exercise or therapy.
“Therapy pool” means a pool that is exclusively used in the physical treatment of a disease, injury, or disorder, and which meets the:
Class E criteria of the ISPSC; or
Definition of “spa” as defined in §B of this regulation.
“Total dynamic head” means the hydraulic calculation of the resistance to flow in a circulation system based on the Hazen-Williams formula set forth in Regulation .38C(1)(a) of this chapter.
“User load” means the maximum number of individuals allowed in a pool or spa, as determined by the Secretary, for sanitary purposes, based on the pool or spa’s water surface area and water depths.
“Wading pool” means a pool with a water depth of 24 inches or less that is intended for use by children.
Water Recreational Attraction.

“Water recreational attraction” means a pool with special water circulation and operational features or unconventional design and operational features which provide patron recreational activity different from that associated with a conventional swimming pool, and which purposefully involves total or partial immersion in the water.
“Water recreational attraction” includes but is not limited to a:
Shallow water pool with permanently installed water play equipment;
Spray pool;
Tube ride;
Water slide; and
Wave pool.
“Water recreational attraction” does not include a pool with limited water features such as a deck-mounted sliding board or a raindrop feature.
“Water slide” means a water-contact amusement ride when the height of the slide is 10 feet or more.
“Wave pool” means a pool designed with mechanical or hydraulic apparatus to generate waves in the pool.

section.heading: Documents Incorporated by Reference.
section.text: The following documents are incorporated by reference in this chapter:

para.text: American National Standard for Public Swimming Pools (ANSI/NSPI-1 2003) except Articles 6.5, 6.5.1, 6.6, 6.6.1, 6.6.2, 6.6.3, 6.8, 6.9.1, 6.9.3, 7.1.6, 7.1.7, 7.1.7.1, 8.1.1, 8.4.2.1, 8.4.2.3, 12.3.1, 12.3.2, 13.2.1, 13.2.3, 15.3, 17.4.1, 17.5.1, 18.6, and 22.2.1, and except that in Appendix E, the term “shall” is substituted for “should” whenever it appears;
American National Standard for Public Spas, (ANSI/NSPI-2 1999), except Articles 7.6 and 7.6.1;
American National Standard for Suction Entrapment Avoidance in Swimming Pools, Wading Pools, Spas, Hot Tubs, and Catch Basins (ANSI/PHTA/ICC-7 2020);
Circulation System Components and Related Materials for Pools, Spas/Hot Tubs (ANSI/NSF Standard-50 1992);
American National Standard for Residential Inground Swimming Pools (ANSI/NSPI-5 1995) including Appendix E, Model Barrier Code for Residential Swimming Pools, Spas, and Hot Tubs;
American National Standard for Aboveground/Onground Residential Swimming Pools (ANSI/NSPI-4 1992);
15 U.S.C. §8003, as amended; and
International Swimming Pool and Spa Code (ISPSC), International Code Council, which has been incorporated by reference in COMAR 09.12.56.03.
Operations and Maintenance Standards. All public pools and spas shall comply with Regulations .01—.04 and .13—.24 of this chapter for operations and maintenance standards.
Construction Permits and Operation Permits. All public pools and spas shall comply with Regulations .05—.12 of this chapter to obtain permits related to construction and operation.
Construction and Design Standards.
Legacy public pools and spas shall comply with Regulations .26—.47 of this chapter for construction and design.
Legacy public pools and spas which have undergone major alteration shall comply with COMAR 09.12.56, the Maryland Swimming Pool and Spa Standards, for construction and design.
Public pools and spas approved and constructed after December 31, 2023 shall comply with COMAR 09.12.56, the Maryland Swimming Pool and Spa Standards, for construction and design.
Exemptions. This chapter does not apply to a:
Private pool, except for a private pool defined as a limited public-use pool in Regulation .02B of this chapter;
Private spa;
Pool or spa that is completely emptied of water, disinfected, and refilled with water between each use and that is intended for use or used by a single individual during each use; or
Pool or spa at a bed and breakfast, if the bed and breakfast facility has eight or fewer guest rooms.
An owner shall comply with:

The provision that establishes a higher standard for the promotion and protection of public health and safety if a provision of this chapter is in conflict with a local code, ordinance, statute, or other regulation; and
This chapter if there is a conflict between this chapter and the provisions of American National Standard for Public Swimming Pools or the American National Standard for Public Spas.

An owner who intends to construct or alter a public pool or spa shall obtain a construction or alteration permit from the Secretary in accordance with this regulation before beginning the construction or alteration.
An owner may not construct or alter a recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa without a construction or alteration permit from the Secretary.
To obtain a construction or alteration permit, an owner shall submit to the Secretary:
An application for a construction or alteration permit on an application form provided by the Secretary that includes:
The full names and addresses of:
The owner; and
Any authorized agents of the owner who may act on the owner’s behalf during the construction or alteration of the pool or spa;

A statement saying “I hereby acknowledge that all items either listed or shown in these plans and specifications as not in contract, by others, or equivalent, are my responsibility. I also realize that this entire project must be completed in accordance with the approved plans and specifications and all conditions listed in the construction or alteration permit and meet the requirements of this chapter prior to the issuance of an operating permit by the Secretary”; and
The owner’s signature, which indicates the owner:
Has supplied the correct information on and with the application; and
Is in agreement with the statement set forth in §C(1)(b) of this regulation;
Plans and specifications for the construction or alteration which:
Are prepared by a licensed or certified professional engineer, architect, draftsman, or a person with extensive experience in the design of pools and spas;
Are drawn:
To scale;
In a professional and accurate manner; and
With sufficient clarity and detailed dimensions to show the nature and character of the work to be performed;
Include specific information on the quality or performance of the material or equipment when necessary to establish conformance with this chapter; and
Are supplied in triplicate as physical documents or as electronic documents; and
The application review fee required by COMAR 10.01.17.02.
Except as provided in §E of this regulation, an owner shall ensure that the plans and specifications required by §C of this regulation include the following:
Site plan with contours;
Building plan;
Pool or spa layout plan, sectional views, and appurtenant equipment;
Pool or spa piping layout plan;
Deck and barrier plan;
Filter room layout plan with the location of equipment and piping;
Ventilation plan;
Bathhouse plan;
Lighting plan;
Potable water supply plumbing diagram;
Waste disposal plumbing diagram;
Finish schedules;
Equipment and material specifications;
Head loss calculations;
Pump performance curve;
Waste water disposal site;
Chemical storage plan; and
Any information, including material samples, necessary to determine if the plans and specifications comply with criteria set forth in this chapter.
An owner shall ensure that, for an alteration, the plans and specifications required by §C of this regulation include the information that pertains to the alteration.
Before beginning construction or alteration work, an owner shall obtain:
Any necessary local zoning approvals;
Building permits;
Electrical permits;
Plumbing permits; and
Any other applicable local permits.

A county’s local health officer may not approve a local building permit for, or that includes, construction or alteration of a recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa unless the plans and specifications for construction or alteration of a public pool or spa have been approved by the Secretary in accordance with this regulation.
The Secretary shall review the plans and application for a construction or alteration permit within 30 business days of receipt of the application.
If plans are submitted that are:
Not in compliance with the requirements of this chapter, the Secretary shall:
Notify the owner of the deficiencies in the application;
Deny the application if additional information to correct the deficiencies in the application is not received within 30 business days of the Department’s request for additional information; or
Allow the owner 30 business days to resubmit information to correct the deficiencies before denying the application in accordance with §I(1)(b) of this regulation; or
In compliance with the requirements of this chapter, the Secretary shall approve the plans and issue a construction or alteration permit, which is valid for:
The start of the construction or alteration for 1 year from the date of issue; and
One additional year from the date construction or alteration begins.

If the Secretary denies the issuance of a construction or alteration permit, an owner shall reapply for a new construction or alteration permit according to §C of this regulation and pay the applicable fees set forth in COMAR 10.01.17.02.
An owner may not deviate from the approved plans and specifications for construction or alteration at a recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa unless:
Revised plans are submitted through the application review process in accordance with §C of this regulation;
The owner pays the applicable fees set for in COMAR 10.01.17.02; and
The Secretary issues a construction or alteration permit for the revised work.

If a recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa is not being constructed or altered in accordance with the approved plans, the Secretary may revoke the construction or alteration permit and the owner shall immediately cease construction or alteration.

If the Secretary denies the issuance of a construction or alteration permit as set forth in §I of this regulation, or revokes a construction or alteration permit as set forth in §L of this regulation, the Secretary shall notify the owner in writing:
Of the reason or reasons for the denial or revocation;

That the owner may request from the Secretary an opportunity for a hearing on the denial or revocation pursuant to State Government Article, Title 10, Subtitle 2, Annotated Code of Maryland, if the owner wishes to contest the denial or revocation; and

That in order to preserve the right to a hearing, the owner shall contact the Department in the manner set forth in the notice within 10 business days of the receipt of the notice of denial or revocation.
An owner shall ensure that a construction or alteration permit is posted in a conspicuous location at the site of construction or alteration.
A person may not operate or permit the use of a recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa that has not received written approval from the Secretary after its construction or alteration.

The Secretary shall conduct an inspection to ensure that a recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa is constructed or altered according to the approved plans and meets the requirements of this chapter, and shall:
Grant written approval for the pool or spa if:
It was constructed or altered according to the approved plans;
It meets the requirements of this chapter; and
The owner has received local approval for any building, electrical, plumbing, or other work that requires a local permit; or
Deny approval for the pool or spa if:
It was not constructed or altered according to the approved plans;
It does not meet the requirements of this chapter; or
The owner has not received local approval for any building, electrical, plumbing, or other work that requires a local permit.
The Secretary shall grant written approval or deny approval of the completed construction or alteration of a public pool or spa within 15 business days of the inspection.

If minor items that do not affect the health or safety of the public need to be corrected, the Secretary may issue a temporary approval for the pool or spa after construction pending full compliance according to the following conditions:

The owner shall fully comply with this chapter within 30 business days thereby obtaining written approval of the recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa in accordance with §B of this regulation; and

If at the end of 30 business days, the Secretary is unable to approve the recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa in accordance with §B of this regulation, the Secretary shall disapprove the construction.
If the Secretary does not grant approval for the pool or spa after it is constructed or altered, the Secretary shall notify the owner in writing:
Of the reason or reasons for the disapproval;
That the owner may request from the Secretary an opportunity for a hearing on the disapproval pursuant to State Government Article, Title 10, Subtitle 2, Annotated Code of Maryland;

That to preserve the right to a hearing, the owner shall submit a written request for a hearing in the manner set forth in the notice to the Secretary within 10 business days of the receipt of the notice of disapproval; and
That the owner shall submit a new plan review application and pay any applicable fees according to Regulation .05 of this chapter.
An owner may replace a component at a recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa before obtaining approval from the Secretary.
Before replacing a component at a recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa, an owner shall obtain necessary:
Local zoning approval;
Building permits;
Electrical permits;
Plumbing permits; and
Any other applicable local permits.

The local health department may approve a local building permit for, or that includes, replacement of a component at a recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa before the replacement application is approved by the Secretary.

An owner shall submit, on a form provided by the Secretary, an application for the replacement of a component at a recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa no later than 10 business days after completing the replacement.

If, during an inspection by the local health department, it is determined that a component has been replaced and the owner failed to submit the form required in §D of this regulation, the owner shall submit the required form to the Department within 10 business days of the local health department’s inspection.
The Secretary shall inspect the replacement of a component at a recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa within 30 business days of receipt of the application.
If, during the inspection, the replacement of a component at a recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa is in compliance with the requirements of this chapter, the Secretary shall:
Provide the owner a copy of the inspection report; and
Issue an approval letter.
If, during the inspection, the replacement of a component at a recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa is not in compliance with the requirements of this chapter, the Secretary shall:
Deny the replacement application; and
Notify the owner:
Of the reason or reasons for the denial;

That the owner may request from the Secretary an opportunity for a hearing on the denial pursuant to State Government Article, Title 10, Subtitle 2, Annotated Code of Maryland, if the owner wishes to contest the denial;

That to preserve the right to a hearing, the owner shall submit a written request for a hearing in the manner set forth in the notice within 10 business days of the receipt of the notice of denial; and

That the owner shall cease operation of a recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa if the component is essential to operation or cease operation of the replaced component, where the replacement of a component was found to violate this chapter until:
The violation is corrected;
A new replacement application and applicable fee is submitted to the Secretary; and
The Secretary inspects and approves the replacement of the component.
Annual Operating Permits.
A person may not operate a public pool or spa without an annual operating permit issued by the Secretary.

In the case of a public pool or spa that has received a temporary approval of construction pursuant to Regulation .06D of this chapter, the Secretary may issue a nontransferable 30-calendar-day permit for the temporary operation of the public pool or spa.
On an application form provided by the Secretary, an owner shall apply to the Secretary for an annual permit to operate a public pool or spa for:
A newly constructed public pool or spa, at least 30 business days before the pool or spa is scheduled to open; or
An existing public pool or spa, 30 business days before the previously issued permit expires.
The Secretary shall:

Issue, for each public pool or spa, a nontransferable permit to an owner whose public pool or spa is in compliance with this chapter as verified by a full compliance inspection completed within the 12 months prior to the expiration of the current operating permit; and
When a public pool or spa does not meet the requirements of this chapter, deny the permit within 30 business days of the receipt of the application by notifying the owner in writing:
Of the reason or reasons for the denial;
Of the action to be taken in order for the public pool or spa to qualify for a permit;
That the owner may request from the Secretary an opportunity for a hearing on this denial pursuant to State Government Article, Title 10, Subtitle 2, Annotated Code of Maryland; and
That to preserve the right to a hearing, the person shall contact the Secretary in the manner set forth by the Department within 10 business days of the receipt of the notice of denial.
A person who operates a public pool or spa shall post the operating permit in a conspicuous place near the entrance to the pool or spa.
Suspension.
The Secretary may:
Suspend an operating permit if an owner violates a requirement of this chapter; or
Summarily suspend an operating permit and close a public pool or spa when protection of the public health, safety, or welfare imperatively requires emergency action.
The Secretary may summarily suspend an operating permit pursuant to §A(1)(b) of this regulation for a:
Critical violation not corrected immediately; or
Major violation not corrected within 24 hours.
Revocation and Permitting After Revocation.
The Secretary may revoke a permit for a public pool or spa for:
Consecutive repeat violations of a requirement of this chapter; or

An owner whose operating permit was revoked within the past 2 years, upon determination that the owner is in violation of the same requirement of this chapter that resulted in the previous revocation.
The Secretary may issue an operating permit for a public pool or spa to an owner whose operating permit was revoked:
After the 6-month waiting period from the date of revocation has expired; and
When the owner:
Corrects the violations;
Applies for an operating permit;
Pays the applicable fees pursuant to COMAR 10.01.17.02; and
Complies with all applicable provisions of this chapter.
Written Notice.

In the case of the summary suspension of a permit pursuant to §A(1)(b) of this regulation, the Secretary shall provide a person with written notice of the violation and an opportunity for a hearing pursuant to State Government Article, Title 10, Subtitle 2, Annotated Code of Maryland.

In the case of a permit suspension pursuant to §A(1)(a) of this regulation or a permit revocation pursuant to §B of this regulation, before taking action against a person, the Secretary shall provide written notice of the facts that warrant the suspension or revocation and an opportunity for a hearing before suspending or revoking the permit.
Hearing. To preserve a right to a hearing, a person shall contact the Secretary within 10 business days of the receipt of the notice in the manner set forth by the Secretary.
The Secretary may enter, at a reasonable time, public or private property for inspecting and investigating conditions relative to the enforcement of this chapter.
A person may not deny or interfere with the Secretary's entry onto public or private property to inspect or to take enforcement action pursuant to this chapter.
Timing of Inspections.
The Secretary shall conduct a full compliance inspection of the public pool or spa relative to the enforcement of this chapter at least once every 12 months.
The Secretary shall conduct an inspection of the public pool or spa relative to the enforcement of this chapter at least once every 90 business days except:
If a critical violation exists, an inspection is required at least every 30 business days; or
If no critical violations were found on the three previous consecutive inspections, only the full compliance inspection prescribed in §C(1) of this regulation is required.

The owner of a public pool or spa that has a structure, equipment, or appurtenance that is not in compliance with this chapter, as determined by the Secretary, may submit to the Secretary for approval a compliance schedule for meeting the requirements of this chapter.
The request from an owner for approval of a compliance schedule shall include:
The reason that the noncompliance item cannot be immediately corrected;
The plan for correction of the noncompliant item; and
The time schedule for the correction of the noncompliant item.
The Secretary may approve the compliance schedule if the:
Owner has submitted a written request for approval of a compliance schedule in accordance with §B of this regulation;
Time schedule for the correction of the noncompliant item is acceptable to the Secretary; and
Operation of the public pool or spa during the time allowed to bring the public pool or spa into compliance does not adversely affect the health and safety of the public.
The Secretary may not approve a compliance schedule for a newly constructed public pool or spa that has not received construction approval in accordance with Regulation .06 of this chapter.
The Secretary shall issue an operating permit or shall refrain from suspending an operating permit to an owner if:
A compliance schedule has been approved by the Secretary for the correction of a noncompliant item;
The owner is following the approved compliance schedule; and
The public pool or spa is otherwise in compliance with this chapter.
An owner who has been granted a variance by the Secretary before February 10, 1997 may continue to operate under that variance.
An owner may request a variance from a requirement of this chapter by submitting a written application that:
Contains specific details of the alternative procedure proposed by the owner;
Specifies the applicable regulation to which the variance pertains;
Explains the reason for the request;
Provides the name and address of the owner;
Provides the name and location of the public pool or spa; and
Demonstrates that the alternative procedure proposed:
Meets or produces the intended effect of the regulation for which the variance is requested; and
Maintains the protection of the health and safety of the individuals using the public pool or spa at or above the level required by the regulation for which the variance is requested.
Upon consideration of an application for a variance, the Secretary may grant the request for a variance if the:
Applicant has submitted an application in accordance with the provisions of §B of this regulation;
Applicant has complied with all other applicable provisions of this chapter;
Application is justified due to physical limitation of the existing layout of the facility; and
Secretary determines that the alternative procedure proposed by the applicant:
Meets or produces the intended effect of the regulation; and
Maintains the protection of the health and safety of the individuals using the facility at or above the level required by the regulation at issue.

The Secretary shall grant or deny an application for a variance in writing and shall mail the decision to the applicant within 60 days of the date the application for a variance is received by the Secretary.
Hearing Regarding Denial of Variance.

If the Secretary denies a variance request that has been made in accordance with the provisions of §B of this regulation, the applicant may file an appeal of the denial in accordance with State Government Article, Title 10, Subtitle 2, Annotated Code of Maryland.
The applicant shall contact the Secretary, in the manner specified by the Secretary, within 10 days of receipt of the denial to preserve a right to a hearing.

section.heading: General Operations, Maintenance, and Required Signage.

para.text: An owner of a public pool or spa shall ensure that:
An inspection of the pool or spa and related facilities is made at least once a week for the purpose of maintaining the pool or spa in compliance with this chapter;
The pool or spa and its related facilities are maintained in a safe, clean, and orderly condition;
A broken, damaged, or malfunctioning fixture is promptly repaired or replaced;
The pool or spa is left in a safe condition when closed for the season;
Pool and spa equipment is installed according to manufacturers' instructions and this chapter; and
An operator completes a Pool and Spa Entrapment Hazards Checklist provided by the Secretary, or an equivalent form, on a daily basis before the pool or spa is open for that day's use.
An owner may make a repair to a recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa in accordance with this chapter without:
Obtaining a construction, alteration, or replacement permit from the Secretary; or
Notifying the Secretary.
Required Signage. A public pool or spa:
Shall ensure that any chemical vat, feeder, pump, or line is labeled to identify the chemical in use;
Shall have a chlorine gas warning sign stating “Danger—Chlorine Gas” posted at the entrance to a chlorine gas feed room and storage area;
Shall have a chemical warning sign that includes the text “Caution! Chemical Storage Area” at the entrance door to a chemical storage area;
May post other warning, health advisory, and safety signs if necessary to protect the public health and safety, for example, “Danger! No Diving In Shallow Water”;
Shall ensure that house rules are posted at the entrance to the pool or spa; and

That is classified as semi-public and does not have a lifeguard on duty shall have a conspicuous sign posted adjacent to entrances to the pool or spa reading “WARNING; NO LIFEGUARD ON DUTY. SWIM AT YOUR OWN RISK. DO NOT SWIM ALONE. CHILDREN UNDER 15 SHOULD NOT USE THE POOL WITHOUT ADULT SUPERVISION.”
Spa Safety Signs.

Public spas shall have a sign which meets the size, color, design, application, symbol, and visual layout of a safety sign set forth in the ANSI Z-535 series of standards for Safety Signs and Colors as included in American National Standard for Public Spas.
A spa safety sign shall be posted in a permanent location adjacent to a spa in compliance with the American National Standard for Public Spas.
The spa safety sign shall include the user load of the spa.
Illumination.
An owner shall ensure that an indoor recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa, or an outdoor recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa utilized during nighttime, is provided with:
Even illumination of the water, deck, and walkways;
Illumination of the water and deck that meets one of the conditions in §A(2) of this regulation;
Lighting that minimizes reflection from the water surface so that the visibility of the pool or spa bottom is not obscured; and
Walkway lighting yielding at least 15 footcandles of light.
The illumination of the water and deck shall either:

Be a combination of underwater and deck lighting so that underwater lighting yields at least 0.5 watt per square foot of water surface area and deck lighting yields at least 0.6 watt per square foot of required deck area or at least 15 footcandles; or

Have overhead lighting yielding at least 2 watts per square foot of required deck area or at least 20 footcandles of light that is directed onto the deck and the water surface so that the entire pool or spa bottom is clearly visible.
Source of Water. An owner of a public pool or spa shall ensure that:
When a public pool or spa is filled with water from a nonpotable source, such as a water tank holding nonpotable water or surface water, the:
Water is filtered, treated, and disinfected after addition to the pool or spa to meet the requirements of Regulation .16 of this chapter; and
Pool or spa is not used until a bacteriological sample taken by the Secretary indicates that there are no coliform organisms in the water; and
Public pool or spa make-up water:
Is from a potable source; and
Which has an iron level over 0.3 ppm is treated to lower the iron level to 0.3 ppm or less before the make-up water is added to a pool or a spa.
Filter Backwash. An owner of a public pool or spa shall ensure that:
The disposal of filter backwash water and pool or spa wastewater conforms with:
Local sanitary code requirements; and
Discharge requirements set forth in COMAR 26.08.01—.04;
Deck drainage disposal conforms with:
COMAR 09.20.01; and
Local plumbing code requirements; and
No filter backwash or other wastewater returns to a pool or spa, except for filter backwash water that has been:
Filtered to remove particulates; and
Treated to eliminate coliform bacteria and waterborne pathogens.

Deck Equipment. An owner shall ensure that an anchor for a fixture used to support a backstroke flag, volleyball net, or similar recreational equipment is fitted with a cap or plug that is flush with the deck when the anchor is not in use.

section.heading: Flow Rate, Recirculation, and Suction Entrapment Prevention.

para.text: Flow Rate.

An owner of a public pool or spa shall ensure that the flow through a circulation system is maintained between the minimum turnover rate and the design capacity of the filter system and associated piping.

For a public pool or spa with a flow rate that is at least 10 percent greater than the design capacity of the filter system or associated piping or at least 10 percent less than the minimum turnover rate as specified in Regulation .38B for legacy pools or spas and during the plan review for ISPSC pools, an operator shall ensure that:
The information required in Regulation .23J(3) of this chapter is recorded in 1-hour intervals; and
Prior to restoring normal circulation, the pool or spa is vacated of all bathers until:
15 minutes after restarting the pump; and
The water quality is verified as not exceeding the limits set for a major violation under Regulation .24B of this chapter.
An owner of a recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa shall ensure that a filter operates within the filter design flow rate.
To prevent a suction entrapment hazard, an operator of a public pool or spa shall ensure that:
A vacuum fitting is capped when not in use;
A vacuum line valve is in the closed position when not in use;
A pool or spa is in compliance with:
Suction outlet covers which are:
Installed, not broken, not cracked, and securely in place; and
Installed according to the manufacturer's​ instructions;
Suction outlet covers which are secured according to manufacturers' directions and in such a way that the covers cannot be removed without the use of tools;
A comprehensive written maintenance program for the pool or spa facility that addresses, at minimum, that:
If a suction outlet cover is cracked or broken, the pump shall be immediately shut off and the cover shall be replaced;
Covers shall be anchored in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications and supplied parts, and only manufacturer specified, noncorrosive fasteners may be used;
Lines and equipment shall be labeled or color coded for ready identification; and
The on/off switch for circulation pumps shall be clearly identified and labeled; and

Ensuring that check valves in the suction line to pumps are removed to allow backflow of water or air to release the suction when the pump is shut off or when an influent blockage detection device is activated; and

If a public pool or spa does not have suction outlets in compliance with §B(3)(a) and (b) of this regulation, the operator of a public pool or spall shall ensure that all pumps are immediately shut off until the pool or spa has been brought into compliance with this regulation.

section.heading: Disinfection, Water Chemistry, and Water Temperature.

para.text: An operator of a public pool or spa shall ensure that a disinfectant or combination of disinfectants is added to the water automatically through an approved chemical feeder to maintain continuously a residual level as specified below:
Free chlorine shall be between:
1.5 ppm and 10.0 ppm in pools for swimming and diving and water recreational attractions;
3.0 ppm and 10.0 ppm in pools for wading or therapy; and
4.0 ppm and 10.0 ppm in spas;
The maximum amount of combined chlorine shall be 0.2 ppm for all public pools and spas;
Total bromine shall be between:
3.0 ppm and 8.0 ppm in pools for swimming and diving and water recreational attractions; and
4.0 ppm and 8.0 ppm in spas and in pools for wading or therapy;
For pools and spas using copper and silver ions as a secondary disinfectant in conjunction with chlorine or bromine as a primary disinfectant:
Copper ions shall be between 0.2 ppm and 1.0 ppm;
Silver ions may not exceed 0.05 ppm;
Free chlorine in combination with copper and silver ions shall be between:
0.5 ppm and 10 ppm in pools for swimming and diving and water recreational attractions; and
1.5 ppm and 10.0 ppm in spas and in a pool for wading or therapy; and
Total bromine in combination with copper and silver ions shall be between:
1.0 ppm and 8.0 ppm in pools for swimming and diving and water recreational attractions; and
3.0 ppm and 8.0 ppm in spas and pools for wading or therapy;
For pools and spas using an ozone generator, the maximum amount of ozone measured 2 inches above the water surface shall be 0.1 ppm;
For pools using PHMB, the minimum level of PHMB shall be 30 ppm; and
For pools and spas using an ultraviolet light/hydrogen peroxide system, the minimum level of hydrogen peroxide shall be 20 ppm.
An operator shall ensure that for public pools and spas using cyanuric acid or a similar chlorine stabilizer, the cyanuric acid is maintained between 30 ppm and 100 ppm.
An owner of a public pool or spa may not use:
PHMB in a pool or spa that uses jets or sprays;
PHMB in conjunction with any halogen compound or ozone;
Cyanuric acid in conjunction with a bromine compound or in an indoor pool or spa; or
An ultraviolet light/hydrogen peroxide system in conjunction with a diatomaceous earth filter.
An operator shall ensure that the water chemistry of a public pool or spa is maintained according to the following requirements:
The pH of the water is maintained between 7.2 and 7.8;
The total alkalinity of the water is maintained between 60 ppm and 180 ppm;
The calcium hardness of the water is maintained between 150 and 400 ppm;
The Langelier Saturation Index of the water is maintained between -0.5 and +0.5 as calculated by:
The Langelier Saturation Index formula: Langelier Saturation Index = pH + TF + CF + AF - 12.1 where:
TF = temperature factor;
CF = calcium hardness factor; and
AF = alkalinity factor; and
The following factor table:
The amount of total dissolved solids is maintained so that it does not exceed 1,500 ppm, except for a salt water pool where the total dissolved solids may not exceed 3,000 ppm;
The amount of dissolved metals is maintained so that it does not exceed the following levels:
Iron, 0.3 ppm;
Manganese, 0.3 ppm; and
Copper, 1.3 ppm; and

The water clarity is maintained so that either a 6 inch seechi disc placed in the deepest part of a pool or spa or the main drain is clearly visible and sharply defined when observed from the side of the pool or spa.
An operator shall ensure that:
Water additives and treatment chemicals are used according to manufacturers' instructions; and
When chemicals are added directly to a pool or spa, no one is allowed in the water until the chemicals are dissolved and diffused throughout the pool or spa.
An operator shall ensure that the water temperature for a heated public pool or spa does not exceed:
88°F for a pool;
104°F for a spa; and
96°F for a therapy pool.
While routine testing is not required on a designated schedule, an owner shall ensure that the water in a public pool or spa:
Has a coliform bacteria level of less than 1 coliform per milliliter; and
Is free of pathogenic organisms.
Deck Surface. An owner of a public pool or spa shall ensure that:
The deck's surface shall be slip resistant or nonskid;
An expansion joint between the coping and deck is sealed with a durable, watertight sealant; and
The deck does not trap dirt or support or harbor algae.
First Aid and Lifesaving Equipment. An owner of a public pool or spa shall ensure that:
A recreational pool is provided with:
A first aid kit as recommended by the American Red Cross;
A face mask for cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR);
Disposable medical grade examination gloves;
A bloodborne pathogen control kit;
A backboard designed for medical emergency use that is equipped with straps and a head immobilizer;
A light, strong rescue pole not less than 10 feet long; and
A rescue tube designed for lifesaving for each required lifeguard;
A public spa is provided with the safety equipment required in §B(1)(a)—(e) of this regulation;
A semipublic spa is provided with the safety equipment required in §B(1)(a)—(d) of this regulation; and
A semipublic pool is provided with a:
Light, strong rescue pole not less than 10 feet long; and
Ring buoy or similar approved floatation device with an attached throwing rope measuring 50 feet in length or 1-1/2 times the width of the pool, whichever is longer.
An owner of a limited public-use pool shall adhere to the safety requirements set forth in Regulation .21 of this chapter.
Telephone. An owner shall ensure that, in case of an emergency, a telephone is available within the public pool or spa enclosure to individuals using a public pool or spa that:
Can directly reach a 911 emergency service without the use of a coin and without connection to an internal switchboard;
Is posted with:
The names and phone numbers of the nearest available police, fire, and ambulance or rescue unit; or
911 or with any numbers necessary to reach a 911 emergency service center directly; and
Is posted with the name and location of the pool or spa facility.
Lifeguard Chair.
An owner shall ensure that a recreational pool is equipped with a lifeguard chair or chairs in compliance with the American National Standard for Public Swimming Pools.
An owner may use a deck-level lifeguard chair in a designated area on the deck adjacent to shallow water instead of an elevated lifeguard chair.
The public pool or spa shall have a locked gate to prevent unauthorized entry to the pool or spa area when appropriate.

An owner of a public pool or spa with a barrier that includes a door or gate designated as a fire egress from a building shall ensure that whenever a lifeguard is not on duty, the pool or spa is secured:
With a cover that has a visible label indicating that it meets ASTM F1346—91; or
By following procedures per a variance issued under Regulation .12 of this chapter.
An owner shall ensure that a recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa has a chemical storage area that:
Is protected against the weather, excess heat, and moisture; and
Has:
A minimum of 20 footcandles of illumination; and
Storage for chemicals in accordance with the material safety data sheet for a particular chemical.
An owner shall ensure that:
A safety data sheet for a potentially hazardous chemical is readily available;
All chemicals are handled, used, stored, and disposed of in accordance with the safety data sheet and all applicable federal, State, and local laws, regulations, and ordinances;
For legacy pools, chemicals are stored in a chemical storage area which is in compliance with Regulation .42 of this chapter; and
For ISPSC pools, chemicals are stored in a chemical storage area which is in compliance with COMAR 09.12.56.

An owner shall ensure that a recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa has an equipment room that has a water-resistant data sheet that is posted in a conspicuous place for each pool or spa and that includes the following information:
Volume of water;
Minimum turnover rate;
Maximum filter capacity;
Water surface area;
Length of water perimeter;
Maximum bather load; and
Operating instructions for valves and equipment.
An owner of a public pool or spa shall ensure that:
Valves, controls, and piping are permanently numbered, labeled, or color-coded to identify their purpose or function; and
Operating instructions for the circulation and water treatment systems:
Refer to the number, label, or color code of the valves, controls, and piping; and
Are posted in the equipment room in a water-resistant cover.
An owner shall ensure that a swimsuit or towel furnished to an individual by the owner of a public pool or spa is:
Washed in a washing machine with laundry detergent in hot water with a temperature of at least 175℉; and
Rinsed in an effective disinfectant or heat dried at 175℉ or more for at least 30 minutes after being washed.

Anti-scald Protection for Showers. An owner of a recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa shall ensure that each shower has an approved pressure-balanced, anti-scald device that limits the delivered water temperature to below 115°F.

section.heading: Special Requirements for Water Recreational Attractions.
section.text: An owner of a water recreational attraction shall ensure that:

para.text: Plans for supervision, attendants, and lifeguards are submitted as part of the construction plans and include safety personnel at all potentially hazardous activity areas; and
The water surface is maintained at a level that allows the surface overflow system to operate properly.

section.heading: Special Requirements for Limited Public-Use Pools.

para.text: An owner of a limited public-use pool shall ensure that:
The following safety equipment is immediately available:
A first aid kit as recommended by the American Red Cross;
A mouth piece for cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR);
Disposable medical grade examination gloves;
A light, strong rescue pole with a rescue hook designed for lifesaving;
A rescue tube for each lifeguard on duty; and
A telephone for reaching 911 emergency services and the telephone location posted with the:
Name and phone number of the nearest available police, fire, and ambulance or rescue unit;
Name of the facility or the name of the owner of the property where the pool is located; and
Location of the pool;
An individual is on duty while the pool is in use who is certified in:
CPR for the professional rescuer; and
First aid; and
Pool chemicals are used and stored in accordance with manufacturers' directions and the material safety data sheet for a particular chemical.
An owner of a family day care home operating a limited public-use pool shall ensure that water safety supervision is provided in compliance with COMAR 13A.15.08.03.
An organized group, agency, or other person using a limited public-use pool for swimming lessons or water safety training shall ensure that water safety supervision is provided as follows:

An individual certified as an American Red Cross Water Safety Instructor, or with an equivalent certification that has been approved by the Secretary, is on-site to conduct swimming lessons or water safety training; and
Aquatic rescue staff are on-site in accordance with §D of this regulation.
An organized group, agency, or other person subject to §C of this regulation shall ensure aquatic rescue staff are on-site in accordance with this section as determined by the specifics of the pool:

An individual certified in American Red Cross Basic Water Rescue, or with equivalent certification as approved by the Secretary, shall be present for each ten bathers, or fraction of ten bathers, if the pool:
Is no more than 3 1/2 feet in depth at the shallow end of the swimming area;
Is no more than 5 feet in depth at the deepest point;

Has a rescue pole that can be practically used to reach beyond the midpoint of the pool and can be used within the pool enclosure without an obstruction, such as a wall or tall fencing, that restricts the use of the pole; and
Has no diving board, sliding board, or recreational play equipment, or the equipment is blocked off to restrict use; or

An individual certified in American Red Cross Lifeguarding, or with an equivalent certification as approved by the Secretary, shall be present for each 25 bathers, or fraction of 25 bathers, if the pool:
Is more than 3 1/2 feet in depth at the shallow end of the swimming area;
Has an area more than 5 feet in depth at the deepest point;

Does not have a rescue pole that can be practically used to reach beyond the midpoint of the pool, or an obstruction, such as a wall or tall fencing, that exists within the pool enclosure that restricts the use of the pole; or
Has a diving board, a sliding board, or recreational play equipment that is not blocked off to restrict use.

Section D of this regulation does not prohibit an organized group, agency, or other person using a limited public-use pool for swimming lessons or water safety training from providing the portable safety equipment, aquatic safety personnel, pool operator, test kits, or other materials required for a limited public-use pool, to meet the requirements of this chapter.
User Load. An owner shall ensure that the:

Number of individuals in a public pool or spa and on the required deck area does not exceed the user load as set forth in Regulation .32 of this chapter for legacy pools and spas and specified during the plan review for ISPSC pools and spas;
Number of individuals using an enclosed pool or spa area or a spectator area is in conformance with local fire code requirements; and
User load of a pool or spa is posted in a conspicuous place at the pool or spa.
Infectious Disease Control.
An owner may not knowingly permit an individual to enter the water of a public pool or spa who has:
An infectious or contagious disease that may be transmitted through water;
An open cut, blister, or other lesion; or
Diarrhea.

An owner may not prohibit an individual from entering the water of a public pool or spa if a physician certifies that the individual's condition is not infectious or contagious by waterborne transmission.
Lifeguards.
An owner of a public pool shall comply with:
Local codes requiring lifeguards if the requirements of the local codes are stricter than the requirements set forth in §C(2)—(5) of this regulation; or
Section C(2)—(5) of this regulation if no local codes exist, or if the local codes requiring lifeguards are not as strict as the requirements of §C(2)—(5) of this regulation.

Except as set forth in §C(1) and (3) of this regulation, an owner of a recreational pool shall have at least one lifeguard on duty on the deck observing the pool while an individual is in the pool, and shall have at the pool:
Lifeguards who are appropriately trained and certified for the type of facility and activity in the pool;
A sufficient number of lifeguards so that a lifeguard is on duty for each group of 50 individuals, or fraction thereof, in the pool; and
In addition to the number of lifeguards required in §C(2)(b) of this regulation, additional lifeguards on duty if:
The shape, dimensions, layout, use, activities, or features of the pool create potential safety hazards;
The vision of the required lifeguard or lifeguards is obstructed;
The capabilities of the individuals using the pool are substandard; or
Another condition exists that compromises the ability of a lifeguard to monitor the pool.

An owner may use a lifeguard on the deck of a swimming pool to monitor an adjacent wading pool, but if a wading pool is the only pool at a facility or if the wading pool cannot be observed from the deck of the swimming pool, the owner shall ensure that lifeguards are provided at the wading pool in accordance with §C(1) and (2) of this regulation.
In addition to meeting the other requirements of this chapter, an owner of a facility specified in the following paragraphs shall ensure that a:
Limited public-use pool has water safety supervision for pool activities in compliance with Regulation .21 of this chapter;
Child care center has water safety supervision for pool activities at a child care center in compliance with COMAR 13A.16.08.05; and
Youth camp has water safety supervision for pool activities at a youth camp in compliance with COMAR 10.16.06.
The owner shall only use or employ a lifeguard who holds a valid lifeguard certification from:
The American Red Cross;
The Boy Scouts of America, not including a lifesaving merit badge;
The YMCA;
Ellis and Associates' National Pool and Waterpark Lifeguard Training; or
An organization that has a lifeguard training program equivalent to the American Red Cross lifeguard training.

Except as set forth in §C(1) and (3) of this regulation, an owner of a semipublic pool that has a water surface area greater than 2,500 square feet or that is part of a multiple pool facility within one enclosure that has a combined water surface area greater than 2,500 square feet shall ensure that at least one lifeguard is on duty on the deck observing a pool in the ratio of one guard per 50 individuals in the water:
During the peak seasonal use of the pool from Memorial Day to Labor Day; and
During the use of an indoor, heated pool throughout the entire year.
Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) and First-Aid Personnel. Except at a semipublic spa, an owner of a recreational pool, public spa, or a limited public use pool shall ensure that:
When the pool or spa is open for use, an individual is present and on-site, holding a valid certification for:
Infant/child/adult or professional rescuer CPR; and
First aid; and
The CPR and first aid certifications of the individual required in §D(1) of this regulation are from:
A national organization offering certification in CPR or first aid, such as the:
American Red Cross;
American Heart Association; or
National Safety Council;
The Emergency Medical Services; or
An organization that has a certification program in CPR or first aid that is approved by one of the organizations listed in §D(2)(a) of this regulation.
Injury or Drowning Reporting. A public pool or spa owner shall ensure that:

An injury, drowning, near drowning, or suction entrapment occurring at a pool or spa that results in death, that requires resuscitation, or admission to a hospital is reported to the Secretary within 24 hours of the incident;
A waterborne illness contracted at a pool or spa is reported to the Secretary within 24 hours of the owner’s knowledge of the incident;
The number of water rescues by aquatic safety personnel is reported to the Secretary every 3 months during operation or at the seasonal closure of the facility, whichever is more frequent; and
The information required in §§E(1)—(3) of this regulation is recorded on a pool and spa injury and illness report form provided by the Secretary.
Standardization.
The Department shall:
Designate one employee related to the enforcement of this chapter for each local health department to serve as the local standardization officer;
Audit local health department pool and spa programs related to the enforcement of this chapter once every 4 years according to the Department’s current audit protocols; and
Provide to the local health department a pool and spa program review final report following an audit conducted pursuant to §F(1)(b) of this regulation.

Local health departments shall submit to the Department responses to any deficiencies within the pool and spa program as identified within the pool and spa program review final report within 30 business days of receipt of the report.

Pool Operator. A person may not act as or perform the duties of a public pool or spa operator without a pool and spa operator certification card issued by the Secretary as required in §§B and G of this regulation.
The Secretary shall issue a 3-year public pool and spa operator certification card only to an individual 16 years old or older who has:

Completed a 14-hour approved public pool and spa operator's course or a course offered by the Secretary with a minimum grade of 70 percent on an approved written examination given following the completion of that course; or
Presented proof of previous certification and has:
Completed an approved 4-hour refresher course; or
Passed a challenge exam offered by the Secretary.
The Secretary may summarily suspend a pool and spa operator's certification if the operator does not comply with §I of this regulation.

Hearing for Summary Suspension. In the case of the summary suspension of certification pursuant to §C of this regulation, the Secretary shall provide the certification card holder with written notice of the suspension and an opportunity for a hearing pursuant to State Government Article, Title 10, Subtitle 2, Annotated Code of Maryland.
To preserve the right to a hearing, the certification card holder shall contact the Secretary in the manner set forth by the Department within 30 days of the receipt of the notice of the suspension.
The Secretary shall recognize a pool and spa operator certification as valid throughout the State.
The Secretary shall issue a 3-year limited public-use pool operator certification card to an individual 16 years old or older who has completed:
An approved 4-hour limited public-use pool operator's course and passed an approved written examination with a minimum grade of 75 percent following completion of the course; or
The requirements of §B of this regulation.

An individual who possesses a public pool and spa operator certification card may perform the duties of a public pool and spa operator at a limited public-use, recreational, or semipublic pool and public spa. An individual who possesses a limited public-use pool operator certification card shall only perform the duties of a limited public-use pool operator at a limited public-use pool.
An owner shall ensure that a certified pool and spa operator:
Is on-site at all times when a recreational pool is open;
Is available at a semipublic pool, public spa, and at a limited public-use pool for performance of all requirements of this chapter and is able to respond to operational problems within:
30 minutes when not available on-site; or
If a contractual certified pool and spa operator, 2 hours when not available on-site;
Measures and records, or supervises and verifies the measurement and recording of, all information required in Regulation §J of this regulation;
Performs all duties related to the operation of a pool or spa as required in this chapter;
Cleans the filtration system when the filter pressure differential reaches a level specified by the equipment's manufacturer or as specified below:
High rate sand filters at 15 psi;
Rapid rate sand filters at 8 psi;
Cartridge filters at 10 psi;
Pressure diatomaceous earth filters at 10 psi; and
Vacuum diatomaceous earth filters at 15 inches of mercury;
Maintains disinfection residuals according to Regulation .16A—C of this chapter;
Maintains water chemistry according to Regulation .16D—G of this chapter; and

Adds a nonstabilized oxidizer into the pool or spa water equivalent to an amount of free chlorine equal to at least 10 times the measured combined chlorine residual plus sufficient free chlorine to oxidize the ammonia and nitrogenous compounds in the water, on a recommended schedule of once per week for a pool and once per day for a wading pool and for a spa.
Facility Documentation. An operator shall maintain operating records on a form provided by the Secretary or an equivalent form and shall:

Except as provided in §J(2) of this regulation, record the information required in §J(3)(a)—(c) of this regulation in 2-hour intervals for a recreational pool and for a public spa, and three times per day for a limited public-use and semipublic pool and record the information required in §J(3)(d)—(i) of this regulation a minimum of three times per day for a public pool and spa, beginning 1/2 hour before opening;
For a public pool or spa where an approved automatic controller is used, record the information required in §J(3) of this regulation:
A minimum of three times per day in conformance with the following schedule:
The first recording of the day shall be made 1/2 hour before the pool or spa opens;
The second recording shall be completed between 12 p.m. and 2 p.m.; and
The final recording shall be completed 2 hours before closing; and
More frequently if required by the Secretary due to conditions such as high bather load, high temperatures, bright sunlight, or inadequate water quality;
Record the following information in the intervals required in §§J(1) and (2) of this regulation:
Disinfectant residual;
Combined chlorine level, if chlorine is used;
pH;
Water clarity;
Water temperature, if heated;
Flow rate;
Filter influent pressure and effluent pressure;
Pump vacuum; and
Total number of bathers;
Record in 1-week intervals for a public pool and in 1-day intervals for a public spa:
Total alkalinity level;
Calcium hardness level; and
Cyanuric acid level, if used;
Record daily for a public pool or spa:
The time of filter backwash or cleaning;
An injury or accident at the pool or spa;
Chemicals added to the water; and
Malfunctioning or broken equipment;
Date and sign each record sheet;
Record the results of the following inspections in the specified intervals to complete a Pool and Spa Entrapment Hazards Checklist:
Daily check before the facility is open to verify that:
Drain covers, vacuum fitting covers, skimmer equalizer covers, and any other suction outlet covers are in place, secure, and unbroken;
Skimmer baskets, weirs, lids, flow adjusters, and suction outlet lines are free of any blockage;
Inlet and return covers or fittings are in place, secure, and unbroken;
Safety warning signs are in place around the pool or spa, including emergency instructions and phone numbers; and
On/off switches for pumps are clearly labeled, and the location of the pumps is clearly identified; and
Check all information required in §J(7)(a) of this regulation before filling a pool or spa with water, after periodic maintenance, and after pool or filter cleaning procedures;
Keep the records on the premises for a minimum of 3 years; and
Submit the records to the Secretary upon request.
In order to comply with the requirements of §J of this regulation, an owner shall ensure that:
One or more of the following is used for measuring the disinfectant level:

A chlorine or bromine test kit that is the DPD (diethyl-p-phenylene diamine) reagent system for measuring free and combined chlorine or total bromine with an indicator range from 0.0 to 10.0 ppm or with procedures for performing a dilution test to achieve readings up to 10.0 ppm;
An ozone test kit that is the indigo trisulfonate method for measuring ozone with an indicator range from 0.0 to 1.0 ppm;
A copper test kit that is accurate to within +/- 0.1 ppm for measuring copper;
A PHMB test kit with an indicator range from 0.0 ppm to 75 ppm; or
A hydrogen peroxide test kit that is the DPD (diethyl-p-phenylene diamine) reagent system with an indicator range from 0.0 to 40 ppm;
A phenol red test is used to measure pH with an indicator range from at least 7.0 to 8.0;
An alkalinity titration test is used to measure alkalinity as milligrams per liter calcium carbonate;
An EDTA (ethylenediamine-tetraacetate) hardness test is used to measure calcium hardness as milligrams per liter calcium carbonate; and
A cyanuric acid test kit with an indicator range from 0 to 100 ppm is used if cyanuric acid is used in the pool or spa.
In order to comply with the requirements of §J of this regulation, an operator may monitor:
Chlorine and bromine residuals by measuring the oxidation-reduction potential (ORP) of the water before the disinfectant injection point; and
The pH with a pH meter.
If an ORP or pH meter is used, an owner shall ensure that:
Periodic calibration is performed on these instruments to ensure accurate measurements; and
Manual measurements are performed on a daily basis.
Critical Violations.

A critical violation is a violation that results from a product, practice, circumstance, or event that creates a situation that requires immediate correction or cessation of operation to prevent injury, illness, or death based on the number of potential injuries and the nature, severity, and duration of the anticipated injury or illness, including but not limited to the conditions of §A(2) of this regulation.
A critical violation includes but is not limited to:
Failure to comply with:
Regulation .07E of this chapter;
Regulation .15A(2) of this chapter
Regulation .15B of this chapter, except §§B(3)(c)—(d);
Regulation .16D(7) of this chapter;
Regulation .16G(2)) of this chapter;
Regulation .17D of this chapter;
Regulation .22C and D of this chapter;
Regulation .23I(1) and (2) of this chapter; or
Manufacturer’s instructions or directions when adding chemicals to a public pool or spa;
A barrier that fails to comply with:
Regulation .17G of this chapter,
For a legacy public pool with a lifeguard on duty, Regulation .34 of this chapter, except for §§A(10)(a)—(d) and B(2);
For a legacy public pool without a lifeguard on duty, Regulation .34 of this chapter except §§A(10)(b)—(d) and B(2); and
For an ISPSC Pool, COMAR 09.12.56;
Meeting both of the following conditions at the same time:
The flow through a circulation system of a public pool or spa meets the criteria for a major violation as specified in §B of this regulation; and
One or more of the water quality parameters meets the criteria for a major violation as specified in §B of this regulation;
A pH level in a public pool or spa that is at or:
Below 6.8; or
Above 8.2;
A free chlorine level in a:
Pool for swimming or diving or a water recreational attraction that is less than 1 ppm;
Wading or therapy pool that is less than 3 ppm; or
Spa that is less than 4 ppm;
A free chlorine level in a public pool or spa that is 11 ppm or greater;
A bromine level in a:
Pool for swimming or diving or a water recreational attraction that is less than 3 ppm; or
Spa, wading pool, or therapy pool that is less than 4 ppm;
A bromine level in a public pool or spa that is 11 ppm or greater;
A temperature in a mechanically heated:
Pool that is above 96°F; or
Spa that is above 104°F;
Hand feeding of any chemicals while patrons are in the water of a public pool or spa; or
Insufficient illumination such that the bottom of the pool or spa is not clearly visible.
Major Violations.
A major violation is a violation which if not corrected within 24 hours could lead to injury, illness, or death, including but not limited to the conditions in §B(2) of this regulation.
A major violation includes but is not limited to:
Failure to comply with:
Regulation .13A(6) of this chapter;
Regulation .13C—D of this chapter;
Regulation .14A(1)(a) of this chapter;
Regulation .16G(1) of this chapter;
Regulation .17B and E of this chapter; or
Regulation .23J of this chapter;
A barrier that fails to comply with:
For a legacy pool, Regulation .34B(2) of this chapter; or
For an ISPSC pool, COMAR 09.12.56;
A circulation system that fails to comply with:
For a legacy pool, Regulation .38 of this chapter; or
For an ISPSC pool, COMAR 09.12.56;
A chemical storage area that fails to comply with:
Regulation .18A and B of this chapter,
For a legacy pool, Regulation .42 of this chapter; or
For an ISPSC pool, COMAR 09.12.56;
The flow through a circulation system of a public pool or spa is:
At least 10 percent greater than the design capacity of the filter system or associated piping; or
At least 10 percent less than the minimum turnover rate as specified in Regulation .38B of this chapter for legacy pools or spas and during the plan review for ISPSC pools;
A pH level in a public pool or spa that is at or:
Below 7; or
Above 8;
A free chlorine level in a pool for swimming or diving or a water recreational attraction that is less than 1.5 ppm;
A free chlorine level in a public pool or spa that is between 10 ppm and 11 ppm;
A bromine level in a public pool or spa that is greater than 8 ppm;
Except for a therapy pool, a mechanically heated public pool temperature between 89°F and 96°F;
A cyanuric acid level greater than 100 ppm; or
A public pool or spa that has a nonfunctioning disinfection system.

section.heading: Pool and Spa Operator’s Course.
section.text: The Secretary shall approve a pool and a spa operator's course based on the following criteria:

para.text: An approved course shall cover general aspects of public pool and spa operation including:
Applicable regulations;
Disease prevention;
Disinfection;
Filtration;
Circulation system components;
General pool and spa equipment;
Operation and maintenance of equipment;
Water chemistry;
Water testing;
Record keeping;
General pool and spa chemicals;
Chemical handling;
Wastewater disposal;
Safety;
Sanitation; and
Other pertinent topics as specified by the Secretary; and
An approved course shall be taught by an individual who has demonstrated to the Secretary:
Expertise in the operational aspects listed in §A of this regulation, as evidenced by combined work experience, training, and formal education; and
Successful completion of an approved public pool and spa operator's course.

section.heading: Standards for Legacy Recreational and Semipublic Pools.
section.text: An owner shall ensure that a legacy recreational or semipublic pool is in compliance with:

para.text: This chapter;
Applicable State and local laws, regulations, and ordinances; and
The American National Standard for Public Swimming Pools.
An owner shall ensure that a legacy public spa is in compliance with:
This chapter;
Applicable State and local laws, regulations, and ordinances; and
The American National Standard for Public Spas.
An owner shall ensure that a legacy public swim spa has:
Clearly identified controls for the swim jets; and
A shut-off switch for the swim jets that is accessible from within the swim spa.
An owner shall ensure that a spa hydrojet circulation system:
Is not connected to a spa filtration system; and
Has a shut-off switch.

section.heading: Standards for Legacy Limited Public-Use Pools.

para.text: Construction. The owner shall ensure that the construction of the legacy pool is in compliance with:
The American National Standard for Residential Inground Swimming Pools, if the pool is constructed in the ground or as a permanent structure in a building; or
The American National Standard for Aboveground/Onground Residential Swimming Pools, if the pool is removable and located aboveground or onground.
Barriers. The owner shall ensure that the barrier around the legacy pool is in compliance with:
Appendix E of the American National Standard for Residential Inground Swimming Pools, if the pool is used by a family day care home; or
Local building codes, if the pool is donated for use by an organized group, agency, or other person for swimming lessons or water safety training.
The pool and the operation of the legacy pool shall be in compliance with this regulation and the following regulations of this chapter:
Regulations .01—.04;
Regulations .08—.12;
Regulation .13A, C and D;
Regulation .14B and C;
Regulation .15B;
Regulation .16;
Regulation .17B—E;
Regulation .18B and D;
Regulation .19A;
Regulation .21;
Regulation .22A—E;
Regulation .23A;
Regulation .24;
Regulations .32 and .33;
Regulation .36C;
Regulation .37;
Regulation .38B(2);
Regulation .41;
Regulation .45; and
Regulation .47.
Circulation System. The owner of a legacy pool shall ensure that the circulation system of the pool includes a properly sized flow meter to indicate the rate of flow.
Diving Area. The owner of a legacy pool shall ensure that the dimensions of a diving area are:
In conformance with Regulation .40B of this chapter; or
If the diving area does not conform to Regulation .40B, the diving equipment is restricted from use by temporary barriers or is removed.
Suction Outlet. A suction outlet is in compliance with Regulation .41 of this chapter to prevent suction entrapment.
Backflow Protection. The owner of a legacy pool shall ensure that the pool has sufficient backflow protection:
For a potable water supply, in conformance with COMAR 09.20.01; and
For wastewater, in conformance with COMAR 09.20.01.

section.heading: Standards for Legacy Water Recreational Attractions.

para.text: An owner shall ensure that a water recreational attraction:
Is designed to eliminate or minimize safety hazards such as entrapment, slipping, abrasions, cuts, falls, trip hazards, impact injury, and drowning;
Is in compliance with applicable State and local laws, regulations, and ordinances, including but not limited to this chapter; and
Has a communication system for use by supervisors, watchers, and lifeguards.
Swimming Pool Slides. An owner shall ensure that any swimming pool slide is in conformance with the American National Standard for Public Swimming Pools and has:
Attachments that firmly anchor the swimming pool slide;
At the end of the slide a minimum water depth of either:

4 feet, or a water depth in conformance with the manufacturer's installation instructions, with a distance of 10 feet along the slide’s centerline for a swimming pool slide that does not slow an individual's entry into the water or that drops the individual into the water; or
